Around that core it fires on pieces that are not ordinary English word-initial vocabulary - foreign words ('sind' 1.35, ' тр' 1.17, ' een' 1.12, ' hast' 1.10, ' zijn' 0.91, ' hebben' 0.88), place- and personal-name pieces ('Bav' 1.33, 'Vienna' 1.25, 'Amsterdam' 1.22, 'Arlington' 1.21, 'Milwaukee' 1.07, ' Heidelberg'), non-word bare continuations ('barg' 1.34, 'unbe' 1.13, 'conven' 1.06, 'rearr' 1.03) and Latinate technical stems ('ocardi' 1.26, ' hep' 1.24, 'ienn' 1.27, 'synthe' 1.01) - while word-initial lowercase English words (' the' -0.02, ' house' -0.14, ' government' -0.17), English words starting with those letters (' enter', ' enjoy'), digits, punctuation, whitespace and code keywords stay at or below zero; it is not a language detector (many short German/Dutch function words are silent: ' het' -0.07, ' op' -0.05, ' und' -0.03) and the class is graded - 20% of word-initial non-English pieces and 19% of word-initial non-word capitalised pieces clear the 0.25-of-max line against 3.7% of word-initial English dictionary words, with some mid-frequency English words firing too (' joy' 0.90, ' spent' 0.73, ' went' 0.59).
